visualReview.notes: Reviewed the corrected turntable and detail views. The east garden entrance shows the projecting gable, triple scalloped balcony arcade, steps and open green gallery. The two Thai halls show orange roof fields with dark borders and gilt ends. Raised links read as part of the same connected group. The roof view leaves the interior light court open.

sharedSurfaceReview.notes: Nine current shared-surface views render cream plaster, blue-grey tiles, orange glazed tiles and dark green timber distinctly. The gable face appears from each applicable view, the repaired porch steps reach the plinth, and the viewer unload check passed.

mediumFiReview.notes: Inspected 25 current frames, including all four authored levels. The long arrangement and distinction between pale blue-grey western roofs and the terracotta Thai roofs remain visible. Close views retain timber joinery, the upper gallery, columns, window crowns and roof ornament.

geographicReview.notes: The native compound perimeter, central court, upper connecting gallery and named separately mapped audience hall set the plan and heading. Inspected the original 384 m field and a current unmasked render. Contact at the east entrance and under the raised gallery reads consistently with the recovered terrain. Exact local steps, footing depths and court grade are approximate.

fidelityReview.scope: Four physically linked halls in present-day Sanam Chandra Palace: Bhimarn Prathom with its western-style garden façade, the southern Aphirom Ruedi wing, gilded Vajariromaya Hall with a Thai layered roof, and the northern raised Samakkhi Mukhamat audience hall. Includes the connecting upper-floor galleries and the open central light court.
fidelityReview.notes: The exact Bhimarn Prathom original guides the east elevation, three-bay balcony and blue-green gallery. The exact corrected Vajariromaya photo guides the patterned Thai roof and gilt portico. Fine Arts Department descriptions and the mapped outline guide the southern Aphirom Ruedi wing and raised Samakkhi Mukhamat hall. Hidden façades, dimensions, interior roof seams and fine ornament are estimates.

imageryReview.notes: Inspected both exact published Qualla public-domain files and matched native SHA-1, published SHA-256 and photographer Ananda’s original dedication. The native source corrects the Samakkhi filename to Vajariromaya. No additional imagery was used.

validation.sharedCaptureScope: Standing four connected inner royal halls at Sanam Chandra Palace, including Bhimarn Prathom, Aphirom Ruedi, Vajariromaya, raised link and Samakkhi Mukhamat.

limitations: The mapped compound perimeter, raised connecting gallery, court and audience hall perimeter are retained. Roof joins, threshold and storey heights, and the division of unmapped individual interiors are medium-fi estimates.

Only the east garden image of Bhimarn Prathom and corrected Vajariromaya original are used. The Aphirom Ruedi elevations and Samakkhi Mukhamat fenestration are inferred from government architectural descriptions and the shared layout.
Fine joinery, roof crest decorations and gable emblems are simplified. Closed windows and doors suggest the standing exterior; interior contents and art are outside the scope.
The original Terrarium terrain remains unchanged. The public grid helps register the connected plinths; doorstep, courtyard, stair and floor elevations are approximate.
